boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all three frozen records in the Chancellorsville Campaign [April-May 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Chancellorsville April 30–May 6, Fredericksburg II May 3 and Salem Church May 3–4, 1863. VA033 and VA034 lie inside VA032's frozen interval; campaign-wide loss tables and Sixth Corps totals span more than one engagement and must not be added or assigned. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen structured bounds (US 97,382; CS 57,352) are imported estimates and remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces for this engagement, whose interval also contains VA033 and VA034.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads 154,734 total (US 97,382; CS 57,352), with matching structured bounds; the live field reads zero. Doubleday gives Hooker about 124,500 of all arms, doubts he had over 113,000 for combat, and relays Forbes's 114,500 effective and 62,000 for Lee; he says Lee's army numbered about 62,000 by Confederate official reports. Lee writes of the enemy's superiority of numbers.
claims.rationale: Rolls, effective estimates and relayed figures differ in scope and source; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Lee says the Union position near Chancellorsville was of great natural strength in dense forest, with log breastworks and felled-tree abatis, and later that Hooker withdrew to a previously fortified position nearer the river. Doubleday says dense thickets broke up every organization that tried to pass them, while the Confederates knew the country and had an entrenched line at Tabernacle Church.
claims.rationale: Natural ground and works built during the interval are combined; boundaries unset and no map verification or numerical terrain effect.

claims.value: Doubleday says Hooker halted and withdrew on May 1 over his generals' objections, then countermanded too late; that Hooker was stunned on May 3 and was manifestly unfit to give orders though he soon resumed command; and that Hooker ordered the retreat on May 4 against the majority of his council. Lee credits Jackson, wounded by his own men, and Stuart, who took his command. The frozen Union commander is Hooker; the frozen Confederate commanders are Lee, as General, and Jackson, as Major General, whom Lee's report calls Lieutenant-General; the live heading ranks Lee Major General.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed to Doubleday and Lee; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit. The heading rank and the frozen Jackson rank are not adopted.

claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. NPS's 'Lee's greatest victory' is a historians' judgment and campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 24,000 total (US 14,000; CS 10,000); the live field reads zero. Doubleday's table of losses, which he says is from the official reports and inaccurate on the Confederate side, totals 17,197 Union (Sixth Corps 4,601) and 13,019 Confederate for the whole campaign.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Doubleday's table includes Sedgwick's and Early's actions (VA033, VA034) and must not be assigned to this engagement or added to theirs; its OCR layout is garbled.

open_questions: Hooker's testimony and dispatches, the corps and division reports, Stuart's and Jackson's corps reports and the medical returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Doubleday is an interested participant history (he commanded a division at Chancellorsville) whose figures partly rest on others' estimates. Lee's, Sedgwick's and Early's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXV, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
